title: Patch: a banned account drops off the public Players list, as it already drops off the ranked leaderboard
thread:
**Issue #3911 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #3911: Patch: a banned account drops off the public Players list, as it already drops off the ranked leaderboard
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The Statistics page has a public Players tab that ranks players by games played. Those numbers come from each player's own browser, so a cheater can send made-up totals and sit at the top. Banning is the moderators' tool, and a ban already takes an account off the ranked leaderboard. It does nothing to the Players tab, though: the banned account keeps its place until someone edits the database by hand. Once this is built, a banned account is left out of the Players tab and its search, and comes back when the ban is lifted.

## Why

- `player_stats_list_public` filters on privacy alone. In Postgres (`crates/server/src/db/pg.rs:6797-6808`) it reads `where ps.is_private = false`, ordered by games, most first. The in-memory store does the same (`crates/server/src/db/fake.rs:3171-3196`, `.filter(|r| !r.is_private)`).
- `GET /api/stats/players` needs no sign-in (`crates/server/src/app.rs:723`, `AuthLevel::None`).
- The counts are the client's (R1771000). `whole_count` (`crates/server/src/api/stats.rs:1544-1551`) accepts any whole number up to 2^53−1, so one hand-made `PUT /api/stats/player` puts an account at the top.
- `moderate ban` only sets `profiles.status` (`crates/server/src/cli/moderate.rs:132-136`). That stops the account writing again, since an Active route refuses a banned profile (`crates/server/src/api/http.rs:811`), but the row stays public.
- R3290000 already keeps a banned account's standing off the public leaderboard, the percentiles and Jlorious (`pg.rs:5718`, `p.status = 'banned' as banned`; `fake.rs:3531`). The Players tab is the one public ranking it doesn't reach.

## Proposal

- The Postgres query adds `and p.status <> 'banned'`, and the in-memory store skips profiles whose status is `ProfileStatus::Banned`.
- A ruling note in the issue's block extends R3290000 to the Players tab, with its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/<N>.md`.
- Unbanning brings the row back. There is no migration, and the stored statistics are untouched.

## Where it lands

- `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs`, `crates/server/src/db/fake.rs`
- `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs`, `crates/server/tests/api/stats.rs`
- `spec/rulings/`, `spec/pending/<N>.md`; SPEC §9.4, §9.12; R3290000, R1771000

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A store contract test, run on both stores: a banned profile with public statistics is absent from `player_stats_list_public`, with and without a search term, and is listed again once unbanned (fails today).
- [ ] An API test: `GET /api/stats/players` leaves the banned profile out.
- [ ] The ruling note lists its proving tests, and `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-server` passes, and `sh crates/server/tests/db/run.sh` covers the Postgres query.

## Size and risks

Small: about 20 lines plus tests and a ruling. Nothing changes for players in good standing. A banned player's own stored copy is kept, so lifting the ban restores their row as it was.
```
